text:
Alex: Heads-up — spun up a canary that separates prefill vs decode paths and wires a small 'batcher-shim' to prefer decode-only batches for streaming requests. Observed a weird regresssion: overall p95 latency for short-chat flows increased ~15% on canary vs baseline. Anyone else see this in profiling?
Kevin: I pulled a quick profile. Noticed increased contention in the token-batcher map during prefill hot spikes. decode path threads are waiting on the same batcher locks more often. Also KV cache eviction rate is higher. p99 GPU occupancy is OK, but CPU scheduling looks noisier.
Sara: Interesting — that matches my run. Splitting queues reduced preferred decode batch formation, but prefill threads are now thrashing the batching controller because they try to assemble large prefix batches, starving small decode batches and causing head-of-line delays.
Mohit: KV perspective: when prefill aggressively tries to warm KV caches it issues many parallel prefetches. On canary we saw a KV cache drain pattern — a lot of short-lived fills and early evictions. Miss rate up ~12%. That increases token lookups during decode and adds CPU work.
Alex: @Kevin can you paste the pprof snippet you used?
Kevin: Sure — here's the top of the flame for the canary run (sanitized):
```
pprof --web /tmp/canary/cpu.pprof
Top cumulative:
  - 32%  runtime.mutexlock
  - 18%  batcher.assemblePrefillBatch
  - 15%  kvcache.fill
  - 10%  scheduler.waitForTokenBudget
```
Feels like two orthogonal issues: lock contention in the batcher and KV churn.
Sara: Proposal: implement a lightweight 'token-fence' that enforces per-phase token budgets and a soft handoff. Key ideas:
- Give decode a reserved token budget slice (e.g., 25% of per-request token budget) so small streaming decodes can form tiny batches without competing with prefill.
- Let prefill be opportunistic but capped by a backpressure window when decode queue depth is above threshold.
- Move the batcher map to a sharded map keyed by (phase, model_shard) to reduce lock hot spots.
Mohit: Also suggest KV changes:
- Add kv-warmup throttling: limit concurrent prefetches per-host and rate limit warmups.
- Eviction grace: keep recently-used KV entries pinned for a short window after prefill completes to avoid immediate eviction when decode starts.
Alex: That sounds reasonable. We need to avoid big config churn though. Can we ship as experiments behind a feature flag and run A/B for 4 hours?
Kevin: I built a shim change that shards the batcher map and implements a cheap try-lock path for decode. Dropped mutex wait in a quick local run. I'll push to canary with feature flag `token-fence+batcher-shim`.
perf-bot: perf-ci: canary run #4125 vs baseline shows throughput delta -8% and p95 latency +12% for the canary. Regression triggered. See: https://perf.example/reports/4125
Sara: Regression makes sense until we add the token-fence + kv-throttle. Current canary only had queue split but no token budgets or kv changes.
Mohit: Action item: add kv-warmup throttle + short pin window (200ms) and token-fence with default conservative values (reserve 20% for decode). Then run a 4h canary with traffic shaping (50% traffic) and collect pprof + kv metrics.
Alex: Plan: revert aggressive prefill changes if regression persists after the full experiment. For now: Kevin push the shim + token-fence flag, Mohit push kv-throttle, Sara add config knobs and dashboards. I'll coordinate canary rollout and guard rails.
Kevin: Pushed new canary branch `canary/token-fence-shim-v2`. Commands I used to run the experiment:
```bash
# start canary with 10% traffic
deploy --env canary --tag canary/token-fence-shim-v2 --traffic 10
# collect pprof after 15m
curl http://canary-host:6060/debug/pprof/profile > /tmp/canary/cpu.pprof
```
Alex: Thanks. Everyone drop short updates here once the 4h run completes. :thumbsup:
Sara: Attached quick config snippet I'll use for the experiment:
```json
{
  "batcher": { "shards": 8, "decode_trylock_fallback_ms": 2 },
  "token_fence": { "decode_reserve_pct": 20, "backpressure_threshold": 10 },
  "kv": { "warmup_concurrency": 4, "pin_window_ms": 200 }
}
```
Mohit: I'll also emit a new kv metric `kv.prefill_prefetches` so we can track warmup pressure.
perf-bot: perf-ci: scheduled long-run collection for canary/token-fence-shim-v2 at +4h.
Alex: Great. If we still see p95 regressions after the full set of fixes we'll roll back prefill aggressiveness and iterate on batcher sharding.
Kevin: Noted.
Sara: Will add dashboard panels for decode queue depth, token budget utilization, kv miss rate.
Mohit: Running a short stress test now with synthetic small-decode workload to validate no head-of-line. Will report back in ~30m.
Alex: Cool — thanks all.
